title: Date and time: `LocalDate`, `Instant`, time zones and durations

videos.script: Time looks simple until a program has to agree with a calendar. {{instant}} An instant is one point on one time line, the same everywhere. What day it was depends on where you stood: the same second was Saturday in São Paulo and Sunday in Tokyo. {{spans}} Then how long. A month after the thirty-first of January is the twenty-eighth of February, and on the night New York moves its clocks, one day is twenty-three hours. {{formats}} Then text. A date printed for a person, a date typed by one, and the single wrong letter in a pattern that prints the next year for the last days of December. {{clock}} And last, the clock itself. Code that asks the system what day it is can only ever be tested today. Pass it a clock instead, and the same rule can be checked on any day you like.
